chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from al-Ḥasan, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from al-Fuḍayl, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: He makes it up during the day, so long as the sun has not passed the zenith, as witr; then when the sun has passed the zenith, then two by two.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, used here to indicate the timing of zawāl
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime period in which the make-up prayer is performed
key_terms.تَزُلِ: passes the zenith, referring to the sun’s decline from midday
key_terms.مَثْنَى مَثْنَى: two by two, meaning in pairs of two rakʿahs
key_terms.وِتْرًا: as witr, meaning an odd-numbered prayer form
key_terms.يَقْضِيهِ: he makes it up, meaning performing the missed prayer later

ai.seo_question: How should missed nawāfil and witr be made up during the day according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on how to make up missed supererogatory prayers and the witr prayer during the daytime. Before zawāl, it is made up as witr, and after zawāl, it is performed in units of two by two.
